newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open with 0.89 percent jump.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open with 0.89 percent jump.

text.p: French shares opened with a near one percent jump on Tuesday on the back of a higher dollar and an 0.6 percent overnight rise on Wall Street, dealers said.

"Everything is looking fine. Confidence is coming back while we are awaiting the U.S. statistics at the end of the week. As long as the dollar holds up, there is no reason why the market should fall," a broker said.
The dollar is at a 34-month high against the mark.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 23.25 points or 0.89 percent at 2,623.51 at 0903 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,634 from 2,606 on Monday's close.

U.S. leading indicators for January are due at 1330 GMT, with economists expecting a 0.5 percent rise. German February unemployment figures, which could show a further rise, are due on Thursday. U.S. February unemployment due on Friday.
Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will testify on the U.S. economy to the House Budget committee at 1500 GMT.
La Tribune newspaper published what it called a blueprint for Alcatel's plan to buy Thomson-CSF from the state with the help of Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation.
Technical analysts saw resistance levels for the CAC-40 future at 2,634, 2,643, 2,655 and 2,664, support at 2,612, 2,601, 2,595, 2,588 and 2,581.

Renault down 1.43 percent at 138 francs on profit taking after its big jump on Thursday and Friday on the back of its Belgian plant closure plan. Some investors now fear a backlash as Belgian government and Renault unions in Belgium, France and Spain brace for a fight.
Brokers IMI Sigeco in London said it was maintaining sell recommendation, "We ... expect Renault shares to reverse the recent outperformance and resume long-term trend of underperformance."
Trading volume was some 750 million francs, of which 588 million in CAC-40 shares.
Sports wear group Salomon SA was biggest riser with 7.38 percent gain to 431 francs. Tobacco group Seita and insurer GAN were among biggest losers.
